objective.text: Loop 6 of the extraction evaluation — repair the shadow-recall instrument before re-asking the ranking questions. C1 has two halves that are one job: lifecycle-state snapshot as of the replayed session, and a candidate pool restricted to entries that existed then. Plus the op-vocabulary ADR (project.version removal leading), with the usage signal displaced to Loop 7. Brief at ~/.agents/mailbox/channels/sia/loop-6-brief.md.

tasks.title: Session identity is keyed per project, not per session
tasks.note: **a reconnect adopts the WRONG session's uuid** NEW (Session 53). `active-session.json` keys on `<project_dir>::<ide>`, so two Claude sessions in one repo share a slot and the later `started_at` wins; v0.21.0's self-registration then adopts the other session's id. Proven live at close-out: 33 `recall_log` rows under this session's real id, and feedback row **#348 under a foreign uuid absent from the `sessions` table**. One live instance of the 106 provenance-broken ratings. **v0.21.0 fixed an absence by introducing a wrong value, which is strictly worse — absence was detectable.** A reconnected server genuinely cannot know its session from a per-project key; the key must carry the session. Row 348 may want correcting. Entry **474**; extends 325 and 461. (Session 53)

tasks.title: The lifecycle bundle's remaining three parts stay BLOCKED
tasks.note: **do not wire `evaluateLifecycle` into the session-end sweep** NEW (Session 53). Ledger's ruling: no defensible apoptosis threshold exists while `success_rate` is a citation rate (`index-v2.ts:110` falls back to a tag-substring topic-mention detector that cannot emit `harmful`). At t=0.3 the gate auto-deletes **22 entries with spotless records**, including one at 77 recalls and entry 351, which describes this exact failure mode. **Part 1 alone is also unsafe** — `success_rate` feeds the ranking penalty at `lifecycle.ts:102`. Second independent blocker: `evaluateLifecycle` is called from exactly one place (`server.ts:736`, `ob_feedback`), so the sweep never evaluates the lifecycle at all. Unblocking measurement is running — read `Research/rating-method-prereg-2026-09-01.md` §4 only after **10 sessions**, and honour §5 on what cannot be concluded. Part 3 unshippable (no objective gating signal exists). Part 4 shipped as v0.23.0. (Session 53)

tasks.title: Add a `/sync` validator that stats every MCP command path in `~/.claude.json`

GitNexus MCP had been **disconnected for an unknown period**: the registration pointed at `C:\Program Files\nodejs\gitnexus.cmd`, which does not exist, while the npm prefix is `AppData\Roaming\npm`. tasks.title: Make point-of-use rating reachable
tasks.note: **`/end` is the wrong and only moment** (Aaron's question, Session 49). Ratings happen once, at `/end`, in a batch where the agent retro-rates a dozen entries long after the reasoning they informed. **Rating at *retrieval* is not the fix** — at recall time you know the match was plausible, not that it helped, so it measures the retriever rather than the knowledge, and retrieval is *already* recorded deterministically (`recall_count`, `last_recalled_at`, `recall_log`: 685 recalls across 175 of 357 entries). The right moment is point-of-use: when an entry demonstrably changes a decision, minutes after recall. **`ob_feedback` is already callable at any time — nothing enforces `/end`.** The actual blocker is that `/start` injects recalled entries as prose without their IDs, so mid-session rating is not *reachable*. Surfacing `[id]` alongside each injected entry is the small deterministic unblock; keep `/end` as the sweep for whatever went unrated in flight. Pairs with the apoptosis item above — earlier timing alone will not produce a "harmful" the rater was never going to give. Current coverage: **104 entries recalled but never rated**, 80 of 357 ever rated.

tasks.title: Replace-on-write for `state` facts
tasks.note: the structural fix deferred from Session 48, and the half that actually stops rot rather than reporting it. A `state` write should replace its predecessor and demote the old value to a `## Log` section in the vault note; `event` keeps appending. The single place to change is `pipelines/store/index.ts` where `writeExperience` returning null currently ends the write. **Gated on real labels**: the classifier is ~50–60% precise on the state side, so replacing on an inferred label would archive history. Wait until `ob_store kind` has produced a meaningful number of recorded labels — `effectiveKind` already prefers them. (Session 48)

tasks.title: Improve state-side classifier precision
tasks.note: **with labels, not regexes** reading all 41 state-classified entries, roughly 15–20 are genuinely state; the rest are lessons that *mention* a path/port/threshold, caught by the `path is` / `threshold is` markers. Separating "about the value" from "mentions the value" is semantic and belongs to the model leg, per the dream-design split. **Do not tune the regexes against the current corpus** — that is fitting to noise on a sample of 41. tasks.title: Add agent attribution to sessions
tasks.note: (Aaron's proposal, Session 41) — records currently carry objective, session id and status but not *which agent* produced them. **Must come from a per-session `--agent` flag, not `.agents/AGENT.md`**: Forge and Probe both read the same AGENT.md in this repo, so deriving it from the project file would label both "Forge" and be actively misleading — exactly the collision that required telling Probe to ignore AGENT.md. Proof of value: `Session_42.md`/`Session_43.md` were stamped with Forge's UUID while written by Probe; an `agent` field would have made that contradiction visible on line 4 instead of costing three mailbox rounds. Pays off in shadow recall too — a builder's queries differ in shape from a researcher's, and pooled scores could mask a ranking that suits one and not the other. Scope: `agent` on the active-session slot + `sessions` table, mirroring the `--ide` plumbing. **Counterpoint to weigh:** agent↔IDE is currently 1:1 per repo, so `ide` already proxies for it; value grows when two agents share an IDE (Atlas and Forge are both Claude Code).

Gate: after ~10 sessions on the v0.19.0 default, read the `ob_stats` trigger census; if `'unspecified'` is non-trivial, prose is failing — move the session-start recall into `cli-bootstrap` so the hook labels it deterministically, composed with the surface-entry-IDs item (same call site). tasks.title: Vault pollution has a preventer but no detector
tasks.note: (Atlas's framing, Session 52). Today's artifacts were found by accident (an /end step happened to list Summaries/), not by a check. Cheap detector: a /sync check counting `ob-server-*` (and any `mkdtemp`-shaped slug) files in the real vault — a filter-shaped leak deserves a counter (#375). Optionally a root-level vitest config (or a guard script) so a repo-root `npx vitest` either loads the real config or refuses to run, instead of silently running unisolated — the guard makes it loud today, but 23 scattered failures are a worse error message than one refusal. (Session 52)

tasks.title: The slot needs an OWNER, not just a timestamp
tasks.note: (Atlas, Session 52 — the durable half of the misattribution incident). The slot is keyed `project::ide`, so two same-IDE sessions on one project share one entry by construction, and v0.16.0's guard checks *age*, not *ownership* — any fresh entry written by anything (including a stray probe) passes and gets adopted. This is the Session 41 "agent attribution" item arrived as a live data-integrity bug. Direction: multi-entry slots (list of `{uuid, started_at}` per key; SessionStart appends/refreshes its own) + `resolveWriteSession` adopts only when exactly ONE fresh entry exists, refusing with a new `'ambiguous-slot'` reason otherwise (the existing NOT-LOGGED warning then tells the agent to register explicitly). Also: never run `cli-bootstrap` manually against the real env — set `OPEN_BRAIN_ACTIVE_SESSION`/HOME overrides, and consider a bootstrap guard refusing to write a `generated` uuid over a fresh real one. (Session 52)

tasks.title: Verify the vault-isolation leak stays closed
tasks.note: **FIXED and SHIPPED as v0.22.1 (`e633fcb`, diagnosed by Atlas, committed by Forge, Session 53). The guard caught its own committer on day one.** The test suite had been writing session summaries into Aaron's **real** Obsidian vault: 13 files named `2026-08-31-ob-server-{slug}.md`, 69 bytes each, frontmatter `project: ob-server-Cz4UxZ` with an empty `sessionId` and a body of `test`. Found at `/end` while listing `Summaries/`. **This is a recurrence with the guard already in place** — `tests/setup-env.ts` has set `OPEN_BRAIN_VAULT_DIR` to a temp vault since the 57-file incident in April, and `vitest.config.ts` loads it. **Root cause — CORRECTED after shipping; the first diagnosis named a real hazard but not the producer.** The demonstrated producer is **`npx vitest` run from the REPO ROOT**: there is no `vitest.config.*` above `open-brain/`, so a root-level run discovers the tests by default glob and loads **no config at all** — `setupFiles` never executes, `OPEN_BRAIN_VAULT_DIR` is never set, and the whole suite runs unisolated against the real vault. Forge's cwd had drifted to the repo root mid-session (a mirror-copy `cd`), so its full-suite runs today wrote the 13 files. Proven twice over: from the root the new guard produced **23 failures**; from `open-brain/`, 688/688 and zero new artifacts. *(Atlas's original diagnosis — `index-v2.test.ts:55`, `skill-scan-runner.test.ts:33`, `apoptosis-reachability.test.ts:138` each `delete` the variable in `afterEach` rather than restoring it, so within a reused worker every later test falls through `paths.ts` to `join(homedir(), …)` — is a **real second path to the same leak** and is also closed by the fix, but it was never shown to have produced a file. Recorded rather than deleted: two independent routes to one silent failure is the point, not a tally of who was right.)* `server.test.ts:16` is the writer in both routes — it runs session-end against `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "ob-server-"))` and `writeSummary` deposits a summary named for the temp project. **Same invariant as the day's other four instances:** an unset `OPEN_BRAIN_VAULT_DIR` *means* "use production", so absent and configured are the same value from inside the resolver and the guard's own removal is unobservable. **Fix, two parts:** (1) `setup-env.ts` re-asserts the override in a global `afterEach`, so no teardown can leave a worker unprotected whatever it does to the variable; (2) `obsidianVaultDir()` throws when running under vitest and the path resolves to the *real* home vault — a synthetic home is still allowed, so `paths.test.ts`'s deliberate fallback assertion is untouched. Structural prevention plus a loud failure, per the v0.15.1 precedent that removing a read is not the same as counting what you no longer read. **Evidence it holds:** typecheck clean, **688 tests / 49 files green** (+1 = the new test pinning the leak), and a full suite run produced **zero** new `ob-server` files. The 13 artifacts were deleted (Aaron approved); 154 legitimate summaries remain. **What is owed next session:** confirm zero `ob-server-*` in `~/Obsidian Vault v2/Summaries/` after a fresh full run from `open-brain/`. **Revised on the /sync question** — the earlier "no check needed" was wrong, because it assumed the throw always runs, and the root-run route is precisely the case where it does not (no config, no setup, and until v0.22.1 no failure either). Two follow-ups, both filed separately: a `/sync` counter for `ob-server-*` in the vault (there is a preventer and still **no detector** — this was found by accident while listing `Summaries/` at `/end`, not by any check), and a root-level vitest config-or-refuse so a root run fails as one clear message instead of 23 scattered ones. **Also noticed, not fixed:** the artifact filenames lowercase (`ob-server-cz4uxz.md`) while the frontmatter preserves case (`ob-server-Cz4UxZ`) — invisible on Windows, two identities on Linux/macOS, the same blind spot already filed against `ob_store` deriving vault folder names from a canonicalized path. (Session 53)

tasks.title: v0.15.1 made a foreign `.recalled-entries.json` writer unreachable *and* uncountable
tasks.note: (Session 50, surfaced by Prime). Prime confirmed it does not write that path, then correctly advised refusing foreign writers loudly anyway — a future harness version is not bound by today's inventory. That property cannot be built as described: v0.15.1's fix was not a `session_id` comparison but the **removal of the read** (precedence: explicit ids → `recall_log` → the file only if the session is unknown → nothing). On the normal path there is no read, so no refusal, so nothing to report. Net effect: **"no foreign writer" and "a foreign writer never looked at" are the same observation from inside the resolver.** This is a fourth instance of the dropped-count invariant above, sitting inside the fix that shipped this morning — the bad case was made unreachable and thereby uncountable. Fix: split observation from authority — a detector that reads the file purely to *report* and never to resolve ids, preserving the structural guarantee that the file cannot influence which entries get rated. Do **not** reopen v0.15.1; the correctness fix is right, this adds detection on top. General form worth carrying: **removing a read is not the same as counting what you no longer read** — structural prevention makes a failure impossible and simultaneously invisible, which is correct while the failure cannot recur and a blind spot the moment a new writer can appear.

tasks.title: Add a `/sync` validator for the `.agents/skills/` frontmatter contract, asserting all three identity sources agree
tasks.note: (Session 50, reported by Prime). Prime's harness loads `<repo>/.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` at boot and found three malformed: `gotchas/` and `seo-optimizer-test/` have a frontmatter `name` that differs from the directory, and `self-improving-agent-guide/SKILL.md` **had no frontmatter at all** so it never loaded — a 192-line architecture document invisible to the router for months (frontmatter added this session; unverified until Prime reboots). Each skill has up to **three** identities — directory name, frontmatter `name`, and the `.agents/skills/INDEX.md` row — and they currently disagree: INDEX.md registers two skills, Prime's loader finds three directories and loads two *different* ones. Neither reader was wrong about its own file; nothing ever checked they described the same set. Validator belongs in `/sync`, **not** the session-end hook — `/sync` is the mandatory pre-commit gate, the hook runs unattended after the fact. Confirmed hand-written, not generated: nothing in the repo writes that path, so there is no emitter to fix instead. **Directory work DONE 2026-08-11** — Aaron greenlit both. `gotchas/` renamed to `self-improving-agent-gotchas/` with INDEX.md's Directory cell updated; all three identity sources now verified in agreement for both remaining skills. `seo-optimizer-test/` moved out of the loader path to `.agents/archive/seo-optimizer-generalized.md` — **archived, not deleted, because the "leftover fixture" call was wrong.** It is the *generalized derivative* of TCM's applied `seo-optimizer` (placeholders instead of the hardcoded domain, `[COMMON]`/`[ARCHITECTURAL]`/`[SUBTLE]` tier annotations, plus a Priority Framework and two checklists existing in no other copy — 87 unique content lines). The `-test` suffix was recording a skill-generalization test *output*. Aaron to decide its permanent home. **Lesson worth keeping:** Forge and Prime independently agreed it was a fixture and the agreement read as corroboration — but both had reasoned from the same three indirect signals (`-test` suffix, absence from INDEX.md, wrong subject for the repo) and **neither had opened the file**. Two readers, one evidence set: the convergence carried no more information than either conclusion alone. Remaining scope of this item is the `/sync` validator itself. Original blocked items were: rename `gotchas/` → `self-improving-agent-gotchas/`, and decide `seo-optimizer-test/` — a Next.js SEO skill in a memory-protocol repo, unregistered in INDEX.md, which both agents read as a leftover test fixture (and which is currently the only skill Prime auto-triggers that no human ever declared). **The rename is cheaper than first assessed** (Prime, verified): INDEX.md's *Skill* column already reads `self-improving-agent-gotchas` and only its *Directory* cell says `gotchas/`, so the rename edits one table cell and lands all three identity sources in agreement — no name reconciliation across the registry. Whoever wrote INDEX.md had already judged `gotchas` too generic.

tasks.title: Watch for the first real `harmful` rating
tasks.note: **the vocabulary is reachable but still unexercised** (Session 50). v0.15.0 made `harmful` expressible and v0.15.2 made the input source observable, but Session 50's own self-evaluation produced **4 helpful / 8 neutral / 0 harmful** — honestly, since nothing recalled actually misled it. That is the correct outcome for one session and **must not be "fixed" by manufacturing a harmful rating to prove the mechanism works**; doing so would corrupt the signal on the day it started working. What to check instead: after several sessions, is the count still exactly zero? A vocabulary nothing ever uses measures nothing, which is the same failure this P0 closed — one layer up, in the rater rather than the schema. Verify by re-running the census, not by watching one session. Note the distinction that kept #184 at neutral: an entry that is *stale but unreferenced* is neutral, not harmful — conflating "wrong content" with "misled me" is how the 445 neutrals got their meaning muddied in the first place.

tasks.title: Add a `/sync` check that `success_rate` agrees with its own counters
tasks.note: (Session 50). The v0.15.0 backfill repaired 26 rows and `updateFeedbackV2` now writes counter and rate together, so they cannot drift *going forward* — but nothing asserts the invariant, and this column has already carried two incompatible formulas' output under one name. Check is cheap: `success_rate` must equal `helpful/(helpful+harmful)`, or be NULL exactly when `helpful+harmful = 0`. This is the piece the Session 49 P1 asked for that Session 50 did not deliver. **Atlas census constraint (Session 52): do NOT change the formula itself in passing.** The current formula makes the lifecycle a ratchet (harmful has fired 2/290; 104 entries at exactly 1.0, 342 NULL, apoptosis-eligible 0) — but the obvious repair, putting neutral in the denominator, is destructive if shipped alone: per-entry mean helpful is 0.311 against the 0.3 apoptosis threshold, so ~half the rated corpus becomes prune-eligible overnight on a rater whose modal verdict is neutral (63.8%). Denominator change, threshold re-tune, and compile-before-prune (WikiSkill deltas by name: *asymmetric rollback*, itself gated on *objective gating* — use names, not numbers, since entries 455 and 456 number the deltas differently) are one change or none. **Fourth component, same bundle (Atlas, Session 52; verified by grep): a working archive write path.** `archived_into` is read as the soft-delete filter in ~15 places (`db-v2.ts`, `server.ts`, `dream/`, `shadow/evaluate.ts`) and **written nowhere** — NULL on all 448 rows; the only removal op is `server.ts:699`/`:760` `DELETE FROM knowledge_index`, a hard delete with no cascade to `recall_log`/`feedback_log`. So any prune today orphans the rating history that justified the prune — compile-before-prune on top of a destructive primitive is an improved decision procedure feeding a shredder. Entry 455's forget escaped orphaning only because it had 0 recalls / 0 ratings (Atlas verified 0 dangling refs across 927 log rows). Full census: `~/Obsidian Vault v2/Research/injection-ablation-prereg-2026-08-31.md` (§11 carries the era split).

tasks.title: GitNexus's incremental analyze is unreliable on this repo
tasks.note: (Session 50). Failed twice in one session with `FTS index 'file_fts' is inconsistent: document for node offset N is missing during delete`, both times self-healing on retry because the aborted run leaves `incrementalInProgress` set and the next run forces a full rebuild. Session 48 hit the same class and RUNBOOK already documents `analyze --repair-fts`. tasks.title: `ob_store` derives the vault folder from a canonicalized path, so it lowercases the project name
tasks.note: (Session 49). `server.ts:537` computes `projectName = effectiveProject.split("/").pop()` from the *canonical* `project_dir`, and `canonicalizeProjectDir` lowercases the **entire string** when it starts with a drive letter — not just the drive. Result: `ob_store` writes `Experiences/self-improving-agent/` while the `store()` pipeline given an explicit project name writes `Experiences/Self-Improving-Agent/`. **Two live rows already differ** — #235 (older) and #365 (stored during this close-out). **Invisible on Windows** because the filesystem is case-insensitive, so both resolve into the one real folder, `checkVaultIndexParity` passes, and nothing dangles. On macOS or Linux this silently creates a **second project folder**, which `skill-scan` reads as a separate project and which reproduces the exact 60-duplicate divergence repaired earlier this same session. The general rule it violates: **a canonical form is for comparison, not for display** — deriving a human-facing name from a lossy identity key reuses a transformation for a purpose it was not built for. Fix: carry the display name separately (the caller already knows it) rather than reconstructing it from the key; then repoint the two existing rows. Related to the P3 cross-platform item — this is a second Windows-only blind spot. Now documented as §10 of the `path-normalization` skill.

tasks.title: `ob_feedback`'s `referenced` argument does not exist
tasks.note: (Session 49). All five `/end` copies instruct `ob_feedback(entry_id, rating, referenced)` at step A14; the registered tool's schema is `{ id, rating }`. The third argument has been silently dropped from every call ever made — MCP ignores unknown properties, so nothing errored and nothing recorded it. Decide which way to close it: either **implement `referenced`** (it is the natural home for the *was it cited* signal the point-of-use item above needs, and distinguishing "recalled and used" from "recalled and ignored" is exactly what the 445 neutrals are hiding), or **strike it from the five command copies**. Do not leave a documented parameter that the tool cannot receive. Same class as the v0.14.0 stats bug: an interface whose failure mode is silence.

The vault has ` D Experiences/Self-Improving-Agent/wikiskill-paper-vs-sia-memory-layer.md` alongside an untracked `Archive/` holding a byte-identical copy (2287 bytes). Stage **both together** — `git add "Archive/" "Experiences/Self-Improving-Agent/wikiskill-paper-vs-sia-memory-layer.md"` — so git records a **rename** and `--follow` traces through it; committing the deletion alone would leave the archive as an untracked file git cannot protect. tasks.title: Retire the mailbox as *transport*, keep it as *archive
tasks.note: * (Aaron's ask, Session 53; spec at `docs/mailbox-transport-retirement-spec.md`). **The protocol is SIA's, the store is not** — reader `pipelines/session-start/agent-identity.ts` (`readMailboxState`), emitter `cli-bootstrap.ts:135–141`, and it **ships to every template consumer** via `project-template/.agents/AGENT.md:5,14–21` and `start.md:54`; the data lives in `~/.agents/`, a separate repo, and `/sync` validates none of it. Note the name collision — `<project>/.agents/` (gitignored, `.gitignore:9`) is not `~/.agents/`. **The archive half works** (26 commits, 25 touching message files, truncate-to-latest ran clean at `6454bbc`); the transport half is obsolete. Session 53 is its own evidence: Aaron hand-carried the inbox file, Forge then reached Atlas live four times, and the live channel **corrected the file twice** (v0.17.0 had already shipped; delta numbering moved from `#5 before #2` to names after 455/456 renumbered) — so the reply committed at `44dfd8b` was stale on both counts *within the session that wrote it*. **Root cause is one function.** In `readMailboxState`, `lastDecision` parses `^## (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})` and sorts — date-aware; `messageCount` counts `^## \[` with no age, ever. The durable half already knows about time and the ephemeral half does not, which is why five dead channels (TCM 2026-04-24, worthit 06-04, nexcrm 06-09, a2a-hub and openlaser 07-22) announce themselves identically to the one live one. **Same dropped-count invariant as the four instances in P1** — a letter has no status field, cannot represent *answered* or *superseded*, so absence of resolution reads as currency. **Fix (deterministic-first rule #2, remove the trigger):** surface a message **only when it postdates its channel's last decision** — no timeout constant, nothing to tune, cannot drift; unparseable headers count as unresolved and are *reported*, not skipped. Then document live `SendMessage` as primary with the mailbox as the fallback for a peer that isn't running, state the durable contract (*if it must survive the session it is a decision or a task, written in that form*), and move the five dead channels under `archive/`. **Stageable today with no code change** — a blank `mailbox_channel` already skips the surface (`AGENT.md:21`); the code change only sets the default. Supersedes the item below, which asked for the same thing from the other end. Do **not** conflate the `AGENT.md` edits with the personalization-leak item in P0 — same file, separate changes. (Session 53)

tasks.title: Look into how checkpoints are tagged
tasks.note: (Aaron, Session 50). `ob_store_chunk` appends the `category` as a tag *and* keeps whatever the caller passed, so Session 50's checkpoint stored `checkpoint, checkpoint, phase-1, ...` — the literal duplicate is visible in the tool's own response. Cosmetic on its face, but tag counts are what `skill-scan` clusters on, and double-counted evidence inflating cluster sizes is precisely the v0.12.0 defect (60 duplicate notes pushing three of five skill proposals over the threshold). **Check whether the duplicate reaches the clustering input before deciding severity** — if `skill-scan` reads distinct tags, this is a display nit; if it reads the raw list, every checkpoint has been counting double for its own category. Worth reviewing the wider question while there: whether `phase-{N}` tags are useful for recall at all, since they are unique per checkpoint and so can never cluster. Start at `ob_store_chunk` in `server.ts` and the tag-insert path in `db-v2.ts`; compare against how `ob_store` handles the same field. Note also that the checkpoint vault filename doubles the phase (`...-phase-1-phase-1.md`) because the key already contains it — same class of duplication, same call.

tasks.title: Scope 4: True self-improving loop for the protocol itself
tasks.note: MVP built (Session 16): protocol health scoring (sync.mjs --score), shadow-recall (session-end.mjs Stage 3), experience-reference tracking (detectReferences + reference_count). Remaining: error-scan pipeline, context efficiency instrumentation, multi-model proposer, content-overlap scoring, lineage tracking. — The Meta-Harness paper (kb #178, `meta-harness-paper-research-2026`) describes an outer loop that proposes *variants* of a harness, evaluates them against metrics, logs results, and iterates. Scopes 1-3 (built in Session 15) are consistency/maintenance tooling — they check "does the documentation match the code?" but do NOT propose improvements to the protocol's effectiveness. Scope 4 is the real self-improving loop: propose changes to how kb_recall ranks results, how session-end.mjs generates summaries, how /start surfaces knowledge, how auto-feedback rates entries — then evaluate whether the change improved actual outcomes. **Prerequisites before starting:** (1) Define metrics — recall precision (% of recalled entries rated helpful), feedback distribution (helpful vs neutral vs harmful), session duration, /end completion rate, knowledge reuse frequency across sessions. (2) Instrument the pipeline — log these metrics automatically per session so the proposer has data to reason about. (3) Re-read the Meta-Harness source material — kb #178 has a high-level summary but may lack implementation detail for the propose→evaluate→log loop mechanics. The full paper (arxiv.org/abs/2603.28052) and the project page (yoonholee.com/meta-harness/) were indexed via context-mode during Session 15 but that index is session-scoped and won't persist. **Ask Aaron:** Before diving in, re-fetch the paper and video transcript (youtube.com/watch?v=61JUHDK-em8) for complete context — the stored kb entry captures findings but not the full algorithmic detail (Section 3: formal loop definition, Appendix A: qualitative proposer behavior, Appendix B: discovered harness examples). The video adds intuition about recursive self-improvement compounding. (4) Design the evaluation harness — what does a "variant" of our protocol look like? Probably a modified session-end.mjs or kb_recall query strategy, tested against historical session data. (5) Design the proposer — an agent with full filesystem access to prior variants' code, scores, and session traces (the Meta-Harness core insight: 10M tokens of diagnostic context vs 26K for compressed methods). **Key distinction from Scopes 1-3:** Scopes 1-3 ask "is the harness internally consistent?" Scope 4 asks "is the harness *good*? Can it be *better*?" This is the difference between linting and optimization. **Open questions:** Should the loop run automatically (expensive, needs guardrails) or be agent-assisted like Scope 3 (cheaper, needs human judgment)? How many sessions of metric data do we need before the proposer has enough signal? Should variants be tested on historical data (replay) or live (A/B)? (Session 15)

gaps.what: One session uuid is written under two different project keys in active-session.json, corrupting project-scoped attribution.
gaps.evidence: Live slot file: uuid d7e514f8-df2a-483c-a8c7-57f2e0a931b0 appears under BOTH 'c:/users/melve/appdata/roaming/cura/5.10/definition_changes::claude' (started_at 2026-09-08T01:39:45Z) and 'c:/users/melve/.claude/projects/c--users-melve/memory::claude' (started_at 2026-09-09T02:01:03Z). Mechanism established from source, not guessed: cli-bootstrap.ts writes the slot under activeSessionKey(canonicalizeProjectDir(cwd), ide) on every SessionStart invocation, and writeActiveSession (shared/active-session.ts) merges into the file by key - it never removes an existing key holding the same uuid. So a session that starts (or resumes) under a second directory gains a second key pointing at one uuid, and both keys then read back as live. Note the two source comments disagree about whether this can happen: cli-bootstrap.ts says 'this hook runs exactly once per session' while active-session.ts says 'every session start - including a resume - rewrites the slot'. Which trigger produced THIS pair is not recoverable: the SessionStart payload carries a 'source' field distinguishing startup/resume/clear, and the slot records payload key NAMES only, never values - the same drop-your-input defect describeWorkspaceDir was written to fix. This is the INVERSE of T-003: T-003 is two sessions sharing one identity, this is one session claiming two projects. T-003's guards (resolveWriteSession preferring the in-memory id, STALE_SESSION_MS refusing old slots) do not address it, because both keys are fresh and both are genuinely this session's uuid. It matters because every measurement in the Loop 7 C1 reconciliation is attributed by session uuid and scoped by project.
gaps.recommended_update: Decide whether a uuid may hold more than one project key at all. If not, writeActiveSession should evict any other key carrying the same uuid before inserting. Either way, store the SessionStart 'source' VALUE in the entry so the trigger is readable next time instead of re-derived.

gaps.evidence: Session 58, first full `npm test` run after the Loop 7 R2 gate landed: 'applyStateOps (Loop 3 writer) > update_task changes fields, refuses status done and refuses a done task (V2)' failed with 'expected [] to deeply equal [ { knowledge_id: 1, ...(2) } ]'. It passed in isolation (`npx vitest run tests/shared/state-writer.test.ts`, 30/30) and passed on the next two full runs (901/901 both times). It touches nothing changed in R2 - the failing assertion is about feedback_log rows, which suggests shared database or temp-directory state leaking between test files rather than a defect in the writer. Recorded because an unrecorded flake is rediscovered later by someone with less context, and because this one surfaced during a run whose result was being used to accept a change.

decisions.title: Refuse the interim ranking cut on evidence, and refuse the opposing result too
decisions.note: no_maturity loses to live, so the brief's precondition for setting matureBoost/provenBoost to 1.0 is not met. maturity_strong wins by +0.0239 and is ALSO refused: helpful ratings promote maturity, so a replay ranked by today's maturity is scored on promotions its own labels caused. A result that favours the hypothesis is not evidence when its mechanism is circular. A negative result is the deliverable; LIFECYCLE_CONFIG unchanged.

decisions.title: Retire .recalled-entries.json rather than harden it
decisions.note: recall_log already records every ob_recall hit against the live session uuid, and has won precedence whenever the session is known since 2026-08-11. The file was a redundant per-project copy that accumulated other sessions' ids without bound (33 entries here: 11 real, 22 from eight earlier sessions, all wearing the running session's id). It never corrupted a rating; its cost was diagnostic. /start no longer writes it; the read path stays for the pre-ob_set_session case, which R3 makes loud. Per-entry provenance explicitly NOT built.

decisions.title: Delete the text that generates a false claim, not just the claim
decisions.note: Knowledge entry 556 asserted that ob_recalled compares the file's session_id. It was written from end.md A14, which described the fallback as if it were the mechanism. Rating 556 harmful and superseding it with 558 removes the entry but leaves the generator standing to mint it again. Loop 5 R4 corrects A14 itself. Deterministic and structural prevention before prompt-level correction.

decisions.title: Amendment vocabulary: which state records can be corrected, and which are append-only
decisions.note:
Decided once rather than one op per incident. The op union grew by accident — update_task exists because someone needed it, update_gap did not because nobody had yet — and Loop 5 hit the consequence twice in one night.

RULE: a record is amendable when its text DESCRIBES SOMETHING STILL BEING LEARNED. A record is append-only when its text IS THE HISTORICAL FACT, so that editing it destroys the thing the record exists to preserve.

Per type:
- TASKS — amendable (open/update/close/reopen). Title and priority are current intent, which legitimately changes. Already correct.
- GAPS — amendable. A gap describes something we do not yet understand, so its text is provisional by construction. The record most needing correction was the one that could not be corrected. IMPLEMENTED this loop: update_gap. The prior workaround (close + re-add) silently minted a new id and reset opened_session, losing the history the gap list exists to keep.
- VERIFIED — claim append-only; evidence appends; status reopens. The claim is what evidence was gathered against, so editing it invalidates that evidence silently while leaving it attached. Already correct; no update_verified.
- DECISIONS — append-only. A decision log records what was decided and when; amending it is not a correction but a rewrite of the record. Supersede with a new decision instead. Already correct; no update_decision. Gap: decisions carry no supersedes field (tasks do), so superseding is convention only.
- OBJECTIVE / HANDOFF / LAST_SESSION — singletons, set wholesale. Already correct.
- PROJECT.VERSION — REMOVE; do not add set_version. No consumer treats it as authoritative: cli.ts:427 and session-start/state-render.ts:14 display it, state-import/index.ts:439,494 copy it, drift-detector.ts:9 + checks-state.ts:73 + checks.ts:783 compare it to package.json and complain, and state-writer.ts:166 prefers package.json with this only as fallback. It is a cached copy of a truth held elsewhere, with a drift branch and two checks existing solely to police the cache. DEFERRED to Loop 7: 7 call sites plus schema, a state.json migration and test updates is larger than the decision.

ID SCHEME, observed while filing this: the Planner's brief assumed the next ADR id was free, but ADR-021..ADR-026 already exist and nextId has since minted D-001..D-003 alongside them, so the list now carries both schemes. This decision took an explicit ADR-027 to avoid widening the split. The generation bug itself stays filed under G-005 — it is an id question, not an amendment one.

decisions.title: No ranking constant changes on one measured alternative beating one incumbent
decisions.note:
Loop 6's repaired instrument made the recency question answerable and recency_strong (0.02/day) was the only strategy to beat live — 21-11-5, +0.0153 nDCG, winning against a presentation bias that favours the incumbent. The constant was still NOT changed.

Reasoning: recency_strong tests ONE alternative point against ONE incumbent. That 0.02 beats 0.005 is evidence the constant is too low. It is not evidence that 0.02 is right — nothing between or beyond was measured, and the optimum could be anywhere above 0.005. Adopting the one other number that happened to be guessed in the strategy list is the 'flipped because the new number is bigger' outcome the loop's own precondition rules out, and it rules it out whether or not the bigger number won.

shadow/index.ts states the same contract independently: changing production constants stays a human decision; the harness only supplies the evidence. The evidence is now worth supplying, which it was not before this loop.

Recommended next measurement: a sweep — 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.04 as separate strategies — to find where the gain turns over. Adoption is Aaron's call.

What the same run did NOT license: no_maturity ties live, and that must not be read as 'maturity boosts are harmless'. See G-013 (feedback_log 31% complete) and G-014 (success_rate ignores neutral).

handoff.pick_up:
FIRST ACTION, two minutes, before Loop 7 scope: amend G-014's evidence with the corpus-wide numbers and give `update_gap` its first live exercise. Session 57 tried and was refused because the MCP server predated the build that added the op — this session's server is new, so it will work. Verify by reading the gap back, not by trusting the success message. The numbers, measured independently by Planner and Forge and agreeing exactly: success_rate is 1.00 for 148 of 151 rated entries (98%); exactly 3 entries in the whole store carry any harmful rating, one created 2026-09-15; corpus totals 495 helpful / 904 neutral / 3 harmful, so neutral is 64.5% of every rating ever given and the score discards all of it; average recall_count by tier is progenitor 2.5 (n=515), proven 8.9 (n=25), mature 38.5 (n=14) — a fifteen-fold gradient showing the entrenchment loop in data rather than by argument.

THEN: Loop 6 is COMPLETE and accepted. Draft PR #7 (https://github.com/melvenac/Self-Improving-Agent/pull/7) is green at 6733201; merging is Aaron's and the branch prunes itself on merge. Do NOT re-do Loop 6 work. Loop 7 is Aaron's to start — read ~/.agents/mailbox/channels/sia/ for the brief before assuming scope. The displaced subject is the usage signal: whether recalled knowledge changes what an agent does.
watch_out: START WITH G-014, not with new instrumentation. The usage signal is already half-built: success_rate excludes neutral (lifecycle.ts:70-73) and harmful is near-unreachable, so `neutral` IS the recall-without-application signal, it is recorded on every rating today, and it is 64.5% of the record. Read the neutral counts before commissioning anything new. STANDING WARNING, Planner-endorsed: do NOT 'fix' this by rating unused entries harmful — not being used is neutral, and collapsing that distinction destroys the only existing signal and re-breaks the harmful rating just after it became reachable.

TWO independent reasons the Loop 6 maturity tie must not be read as 'the boosts are harmless', and both belong in Loop 7's framing: G-013 says the instrument cannot answer because feedback_log is 31% complete; G-014 says the signal it would measure is degenerate anyway. No maturity constant should move on Loop 6's numbers.

A rebuilt MCP server does not take effect until reconnect or a fresh session. Session 57 shipped `update_gap`, then could not use it — the running server's schema rejected the op and refused the batch atomically. It refused loudly, which is the good case; the memory warns a stale server can instead report success while silently stripping a new parameter. Verify any newly-added op or parameter by reading the row back.

A replay harness must parameterise EVERY present-tense input — corpus membership, mutable signal values, and the clock. Loop 6 found three in one subsystem. The clock hid longest because nothing about the string 'now' looks like state. Check for a fourth before trusting any new replay number.

COALESCE is wrong for a nullable override: a snapshotted success_rate of NULL means 'unrated then' and ranks differently from every number, so substitution must test PRESENCE (CASE WHEN ov.id IS NOT NULL). This was the one brief instruction last loop that would have shipped a correctness defect rather than a doc error.

Bare `npx vitest` from the repo root loads no config — open-brain/vitest.config.ts:8 carries setupFiles — so OPEN_BRAIN_VAULT_DIR stays unset and 36 tests fail on a vault guard. Use `npm test` from the repo root (package.json:7 delegates), or vitest from open-brain/.
Fetch before reading any SHA off this working copy. Local master sat at 8aa2f2b (PR #5) while origin/master was 29e82b4 through most of session 57.
Two loops have now shipped untagged at 0.31.0. Deliberate both times, but it compounds — G-012 should settle it before a third.
open_questions: Loop 7's actual scope is Aaron's to set. Candidates in priority order: G-014 (the usage signal, already instrumented), G-012 (project.version removal, 7 call sites — decided in ADR-027, unblocks tagging), T-003 (session identity per project not per session, scheduled by the Planner), G-013 (accept historical maturity is unanswerable, or instrument recall_log going forward).
Should recencyDecayPerDay move, and to what? ADR-028 refused 0.02 on one-point evidence and recommends a sweep at 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.04. Aaron's call, and it needs the sweep run first.

Should maturity ever be demoted? evaluateLifecycle advances and never walks back, so an entry promoted while its rate was high stays promoted after it collapses. Pinned as production behaviour in tests this loop, not endorsed.
